req.title: Login required for update
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /<id>/update.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-013 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users attempting GET /<id>/update are redirected to /auth/login. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — anonymous GET on a valid post id redirects to /auth/login with status 302; (2) negative — authenticated user GET on their own post returns 200 (no redirect); (3) boundary — anonymous GET on post id=1 (lowest valid id in dataset) still redirects, confirming the guard fires regardless of id value. Each test asserts exact status codes and Location headers to kill comparison-operator and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Application initialised with TESTING=True and pre-loaded database
Post id=2 exists in the database (author_id=1, user Rahul)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login()

tests.name: test_authenticated_owner_get_update_returns_200
preconditions: Application initialised with TESTING=True and pre-loaded database
Post id=2 exists and is authored by Rahul (author_id=1)
actions: Send GET /2/update with the authenticated session
expected: GET /2/update returns HTTP 200 (no redirect to login)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_authenticated_owner_get_update_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    assert login_r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.headers.get('Location') != '/auth/login'

test_authenticated_owner_get_update_returns_200()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_get_update_boundary_id_1_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers['Location']
    assert location == '/auth/login'
    assert location != '/'
    assert location != '/auth/register'

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_update_redirect_does_not_return_200
preconditions: Application initialised with TESTING=True and pre-loaded database
Post id=20 exists (highest id in pre-loaded dataset)
actions: Follow redirect (allow_redirects=True) and inspect final response
expected: After following redirect, final status is 200 and response body contains login form
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_get_update_redirect_does_not_return_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/20/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    r2 = client.get('/20/update', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert b'Log In' in r2.data
